literature_notes: All three ledger lines (L1, L2, L3) describe the same CNNM4-FLAG construct expressed from pCMV-Tag 4 (Agilent), a vector that appends FLAG to the C-terminus. CNNM4's C-terminus (residue 775, I) lies within the intracellular domain (residues 290–775 per the authoritative topology landmarks). The paper used this construct to confirm basolateral membrane localization by co-immunofluorescence with Na⁺/K⁺ ATPase — a standard intracellular-face marker detected after cell permeabilization — not to demonstrate extracellular epitope accessibility. The FLAG tag is therefore on the cytoplasmic face and does not qualify as an extracellular surface tag site. No other ledger line reports an insertion at the extracellular N-terminus (after signal-peptide cleavage at residue 37, mature N-terminus Q38), in the large ectodomain (38–185), or in the short extracellular loop (262–268). Zero sites qualify.

literature_other_positions.note: pCMV-Tag 4 appends FLAG to the C-terminus of CNNM4; residue 775 (I) is within the intracellular domain (290–775), so this tag faces the cytoplasm, not the extracellular surface.
